claim: Alternative protein companies raised USD 881 million in 2025, the first year below USD 1 billion since 2018, according to GFI's analysis of Net Zero Insights data.
quote: The alternative protein industry raised $881 million in investments in 2025
notes: GFI is an advocacy organisation; it warns that recent figures may differ from earlier ones as the dataset is refined. Down about 20% on 2024 (HSC-10).

claim: In 2025 plant-based companies raised USD 450 million, fermentation companies USD 357 million and cultivated meat and seafood companies USD 74 million.
quote: In 2025, plant-based companies raised $450 million, fermentation companies raised $357 million, and cultivated meat and seafood companies raised $74 million.
notes: USD 100 million of the plant-based total was one debt round for Beyond Meat; without it plant-based growth was about 2% (HSC-10). Cultivated is USD 73.9 million in FTB-24 text. Europe-headquartered companies raised USD 418 million against USD 347 million for North America, the second year Europe led (HSC-10).

claim: Investment peaked in 2021 at about USD 7 billion; GFI's current series gives about USD 6.9 billion, against USD 5.0 billion that GFI reported at the time.
source_ids: HSC-10; PRC-04; PRC-02; PRC-03; FTB-17; FTB-24
quote: global alternative protein companies secured $5 billion in disclosed investments in 2021
notes: Current pillar charts give 3.8 + 1.8 + 1.5 = about 7.1 billion (rounded values). The upward revision mainly adds money raised by publicly traded companies (USD 1.5 billion of plant-based in 2021, PRC-02). Give both figures; do not average. Plant-based alone peaked at about USD 3.8 billion in 2021 (PRC-02). Later years were also revised: 2023 was first published as USD 1.6 billion (907, 515 and 226 million by pillar, PRC-03) and now reads about USD 1.58 billion (854, 456 and 267 million).

claim: In the first half of 2026 alternative protein companies raised USD 359 million (fermentation 252, plant-based 65, cultivated 42), taking the total since 2017 to over USD 19.5 billion (plant-based about 10.7, fermentation 5.4, cultivated 3.4 billion).
quote: bringing total investments since 2017 to over $19.5 billion
notes: H1 and cumulative pillar values read from GFI's summary table image (PRC-01); Q2 2026 alone was USD 197 million. Table header reads 2017 to Q1 2026 while page text includes H1 2026; our sum of annual values is about 19.6 billion, consistent within rounding. Privately held companies raised 16.7 billion and publicly traded 2.7 billion since 2016 (FTB-17).

claim: Cultivated meat and seafood investment rose from USD 60 million in 2019 to about USD 1.5 billion in 2021, then fell to USD 74 million in 2025, about 95% below the peak.
quote: Companies operating primarily in the cultivated meat ecosystem raised $73.9 million in 2025
notes: 2019 and 2021 values read from GFI's chart (2021 printed as $1.5B). Percentage is our calculation. All cultivated capital was raised by privately held companies.

claim: Fermentation companies raised about USD 1.8 billion in 2021 and USD 357 million in 2025, but precision fermentation's share of fermentation funding rose from 33% in 2023 to 66% in 2025.
quote: increased their share of fermentation funding from 33 percent in 2023 to 66 percent in 2025
notes: 2021 read from GFI's chart ($1.8B). Cumulative fermentation investment since 2016 USD 5.2 billion. Largest 2025 deals: EVERY USD 55 million, Formo USD 36 million, The Protein Brewery USD 35 million.

claim: Asia-Pacific companies attract a small share of private alternative protein money: in 2025 APAC fermentation companies raised USD 12 million and APAC cultivated companies USD 4.7 million.
quote: APAC $12MM (2025 invested capital); $229MM (2016-2024)
notes: Read from GFI regional charts (fermentation). Cultivated APAC 2016 to 2024: USD 227 million. No APAC plant-based investment figure for 2025 was found; GFI APAC totals are behind a download form (CAP-52).

claim: The Impossible Burger, a plant-based burger coloured with a fermentation-made heme protein, first went on sale at Momofuku Nishi in New York on 27 July 2016.
quote: it will introduce the Impossible Burger on Wednesday, July 27, at Momofuku Nishi in Manhattan
notes: Company press release dated 26 July 2016. The heme protein (soy leghemoglobin) is made by precision fermentation (FTB-17 GRAS table).

claim: Beyond Meat priced its initial public offering at USD 25 a share on 1 May 2019 and began trading on Nasdaq on 2 May 2019.
quote: $25.00 per share
notes: 9,625,000 shares offered. First-day price movement not checked in this wave.

claim: Beyond Meat's net revenue fell from a peak of USD 464.7 million in 2021 to USD 326.5 million in 2024 and USD 275.5 million in 2025, down 15.6% in a year and about 41% below the peak.
quote: Net revenues were $275.5 million, a decrease of 15.6% year-over-year
notes: 2021 peak from GLB-46 (StockAnalysis, from SEC filings; Medium). The 41% fall is our calculation. Beyond Meat also stopped operating in China in 2025 (USD 5.8 million cessation expenses, PRC-06; AIS-45) and is repositioning as 'Beyond The Plant Protein Company'.

claim: In October 2025 Beyond Meat swapped USD 1.11 billion of convertible notes due 2027 for USD 209 million of new secured notes due 2030 plus about 316 million new shares.
unit: USD million; USD million; million shares
quote: $1,114,603,000 in aggregate principal amount of the Existing Convertible Notes were validly tendered
notes: 96.92% of the notes were tendered; early settlement 15 Oct 2025, completion 30 Oct 2025 (PRC-06). Beyond Meat booked a USD 548.7 million non-cash gain, so its reported 2025 net income (USD 219.9 million) is not an operating profit.

claim: In the United States, retail sales of plant-based meat and seafood fell from USD 1.4 billion in 2021 to USD 1.0 billion in 2025, and the share of households buying it fell from 19% to 11%.
quote: package app-ag AG.1: retail dollar sales 1.4 USD billion (2021) and 1.0 USD billion (2025); household penetration 19 and 11 percent
notes: Reused from app-ag (SPINS and Circana data via GFI). Unit sales fell from 281 million to 173 million.

claim: Global retail sales of plant-based foods were about USD 28.9 billion in 2025, up 3% on 2024; plant-based meat and seafood were USD 6.6 billion of this.
quote: Global retail sales of plant-based meat, seafood, milk, yogurt, ice cream, and cheese reached an estimated $28.9 billion in 2025
notes: Euromonitor data via GFI. About 83% of plant-based meat and seafood sales are in Europe and North America (GLB-05).

claim: Plant-based dairy is the largest plant-based category, at about USD 22.7 billion of global retail sales in 2025, and Asia-Pacific accounts for over a third of it.
quote: APAC was estimated to account for over one-third of plant-based dairy sales
notes: GFI APAC via Euromonitor. Caution: 22.7 (dairy) plus 6.6 (meat and seafood) exceeds the 28.9 headline, so category scopes differ between GFI publications; do not add them.

claim: The exceptions to the fade were familiar products: plant milk took 13% of US milk dollar sales in 2025 (16% in 2021) and 9.9% of German milk and dairy drink sales value in 2024, while German sales volume of tofu, tempeh and seitan rose 16.7% in 2024.
quote: package app-ag AG.1: plant-based milk share of total milk dollar sales 13 percent (2025); tofu, tempeh and seitan sales volume change 16.7 percent (2024)
notes: Reused from app-ag. By contrast US plant-based meat was 0.7% of meat dollar sales in 2025 and German plant-based meat volume fell 1.7% in 2025 (GLB-08).

claim: Oatly's revenue grew 4.7% to USD 862.5 million in 2025, its first full year of positive adjusted EBITDA, although it still made a net loss of USD 152.8 million.
quote: I am proud to report that we drove profitable growth in both the fourth quarter and the full year.
notes: Constant-currency growth 2.2%. 'Profitability' refers to adjusted EBITDA (USD 6.8 million), not net profit.

claim: Several cultivated meat firms closed in 2024 and 2025 because they could not raise more capital, including SCiFi Foods (2024), Upstream Foods, CellRev and Meatable (2025), and Believer Meats, which filed for bankruptcy weeks after US approval of a plant that had cost USD 154 million.
quote: their facility costs had grown to $154 million, about 11% over initial projections
notes: GFI counted 142 cultivated companies in 2025 against 155 in 2024 (mergers plus 'a handful of closures'). GFI dates Believer's USDA grant of inspection to October in one passage and November in another; FoodNavigator says the plant 'shuttered in December 2025'. Vow (Australia) cut about 30% of staff in 2025 (NOV-16).

claim: Although 10 safety evaluations of cultivated meat products had been completed by 2025, only three companies (Wildtype, GOOD Meat and Vow) had consistently sustained sales that year.
quote: only three companies (WildType, GOOD Meat, and Vow) had consistently sustained sales in 2025
notes: GFI (advocacy). No sales volumes are published. The largest reported cultivated production run is 20,000 L (Vow, Sydney).

claim: Meati, a US mycoprotein company, went bankrupt in 2025 despite commercial production, and its fermentation assets, valued at USD 15 to 20 million, sold for USD 75,000 in 2026.
quote: Meati's bankruptcy in 2025, despite commercial production
notes: The asset buyers (Ayana Bio and Zenfold) are moving the equipment to India (FTB-38). Gas-fermentation start-ups NovoNutrients and Arkeon also closed in 2025 (FTG-10; FTG-11).

claim: Market forecasts made during the boom overshot: Barclays forecast in 2019 an alternative meat market of USD 140 billion by 2029, against USD 6.6 billion of plant-based meat and seafood retail sales in 2025.
quote: package app-ag AG.5: Barclays 2019, USD 140 billion, about 10% of a USD 1.4 trillion meat market
notes: Reused from app-ag. Cited only as an example of a forecast that overshot, not as a finding.

claim: Singapore had approved 18 novel foods by August 2026, including six cultivated products, from the world's first cultivated chicken (dated 26 November 2020) to the first cultivated beef (Aleph Farms, 22 July 2026).
quote: Singapore has approved 18 novel foods, including the world's first cultivated duck and beef
notes: Reused from app-n (SFA list dated 14 August 2026). The Aleph Farms approval was announced on 4 August 2026.

claim: The United States has cleared five cultivated products (UPSIDE Foods chicken 2022, GOOD Meat chicken 2023, and Mission Barns pork fat, Wildtype salmon and Believer Meats chicken in 2025); worldwide seven companies are cleared for human food, in Singapore, the US, Australia and New Zealand, and Israel.
quote: a total of seven companies have received regulatory clearance
notes: US meat and poultry also need USDA inspection; seafood is FDA only. Israel approved Aleph Farms' beef around January 2024 (RGN-18, secondary). Australia and New Zealand approved Vow's quail in 2025.

claim: The first applications to authorise cultivated meat in the European Union came from Gourmey (now PARIMA) for duck foie gras on 29 July 2024 and from Mosa Meat for cultivated beef fat in January 2025.
quote: This is the first time a company has sought novel food approval for cultivated food from the European Commission.
notes: Gourmey filed in parallel in the US, UK, Switzerland and Singapore and merged with Vital Meat to form PARIMA in 2025 (FTB-24). Mosa Meat date to recheck: our page read showed 22 January 2024, but trade press on the same news is dated 22 January 2025.

claim: Europe's first cultivated meat application was made in Switzerland (Aleph Farms with Migros, July 2023), but no cultivated meat had been authorised in the European Union or Switzerland by September 2026.
quote: the First-ever Submission for Cultivated Meat in Europe
notes: Gourmey also filed in Switzerland in July 2024. Absence of authorisation rests on FoodNavigator (February 2026), GFI (April 2026) and approvals news to 1 September 2026 (HSC-12): absence of evidence, not a registry check.

claim: The European Union authorised its first mycelium (fungal biomass) protein, The Protein Brewery's Fermotein, in June 2026, after a positive EFSA opinion in December 2025.
quote: received the EU's first positive European Food Safety Authority scientific opinion for a new mycoprotein ingredient
notes: The June 2026 authorisation is from a trade press headline dated 17 June 2026 (HSC-12); the implementing regulation was not read.

claim: In the UK, Meatly's cultivated chicken was approved for pet food in July 2024 and went on sale on 7 February 2025 in a dog treat at a Pets at Home store in London, the first pet food with cultivated meat sold anywhere.
quote: the first retailer to sell pet food made from cultivated meat globally
notes: Pet food route, not human food. Share of cultivated chicken in the product not stated.

claim: The UK Food Standards Agency launched a GBP 1.6 million, two-year regulatory sandbox for cell-cultivated products in March 2025 with eight companies, aiming to complete two safety assessments by 2027.
quote: We're confident the programme will meet all its objectives by 2027.
notes: Participants: Hoxton Farms, Roslin Technologies, Uncommon Bio, Mosa Meat, Gourmey, Vital Meat, BlueNalu, Vow. In July 2025 the FSA validated PARIMA's foie gras application, the first UK cultivated application to reach full risk assessment; validation is not authorisation (FTB-24).

claim: US regulators sent 10 'no questions' letters for fermentation-made food ingredients in 2025 (8 precision-fermented, 2 biomass), three of them to Chinese companies.
quote: Fermentation GRAS 'no questions' letters in 2025 (GFI table from the FDA GRAS Notices Inventory)
notes: Includes one supplemental letter (Oobli). No all-years count found. The FDA proposed a rule to tighten GRAS oversight on 10 Aug 2026 (EXP-45).

claim: China's National Health Commission approved a Fusarium mycoprotein and its first ingredient from a genetically modified microorganism in 2025; by July 2025 it had accepted 26 novel food applications, but none for cultivated meat.
quote: As of July 2025, the NHC had accepted 26 novel food applications
notes: GFI says the NHC is working on cultivated meat guidelines but had 'not yet accepted any applications for product approvals'.

claim: Italy's Law 172 of 1 December 2023, in force from 16 December 2023, bans producing and marketing food and feed made from vertebrate cell cultures and bans meat names for processed plant-protein products.
quote: divieto di produzione e di immissione sul mercato di alimenti e mangimi costituiti, isolati o prodotti a partire da colture cellulari
notes: Title and dates from the Gazzetta Ufficiale; article text not read. Trade press describes it as banning 'production, sale and import' (PRC-19); import is not in the title.

claim: Hungary's parliament voted in November 2025 to ban cultivated meat (140 for, 10 against, 18 abstentions), the EU's second national ban after Italy, despite the European Commission finding such a ban unjustified.
quote: The motion passed with 140 in support, 10 against, and 18 abstentions
notes: Commission view via the EU TRIS notification process (FTB-24). Austria's 2025 coalition agreement also commits to opposing EU approval of cultivated meat (FTB-24). Exact vote and entry-into-force dates not found.

claim: By the end of 2025 seven US states had banned or paused cultivated meat sales: Florida and Alabama (bans, 2024); Mississippi, Montana and Nebraska (bans, 2025); Indiana (moratorium to 30 June 2027) and Texas (two-year ban to 1 September 2027), both 2025.
quote: seven states had temporary or indefinite cultivated meat bans in place by the end of 2025
notes: Our read of the NALC compilation (HSC-35) listed Florida and Alabama under 2025; GFI and CSG Midwest date them to 2024, which is the enactment year. Lawsuits by UPSIDE Foods (Florida) and by UPSIDE Foods and Wildtype (Texas) are ongoing.

claim: South Dakota became the eighth US state to restrict cultivated meat, with a temporary sales ban from 1 July 2026; Mississippi also banned cultivated dairy from the same date, and 21 states have alternative protein labelling laws.
quote: Temporarily prohibits the manufacture, sale, or distribution of any product containing cell-cultured protein
notes: End date differs: 30 June 2031 (CSG Midwest, PRC-16) or 30 June 2030 (NALC, PRC-17); give both. Labelling count as of 7 April 2026 (HSC-35). Other 2026 state laws outside the Midwest were not searched exhaustively.

claim: The EU's 'veggie burger' debate ended with Regulation (EU) 2026/1739, which reserves 31 meat terms such as 'steak', 'bacon' and 'chicken' for animal products from 19 August 2029 but still allows 'burger', 'sausage' and 'nuggets'.
quote: Its meat-designation provisions apply from August 19, 2029.
notes: Parliament voted 355 to 247 in October 2025 for a wider ban; trilogue deal 5 March 2026 (PRC-20; PRC-22 says February); published 29 July 2026, in force 18 August 2026 (PRC-21; PRC-22 says 19 August). Terms also apply to fermentation-made and cultivated products (PRC-20; FTB-17). In July 2026 some MEPs tabled amendments to extend the ban to 'burger', 'sausage' and 'nugget' in the post-2027 farm market reform; committee vote expected 1 December 2026, plenary in 2027 (PRC-21; PRC-22).

claim: Denmark's Action Plan for Plant-based Foods (October 2023) set up a Plant-based Food Grant of DKK 675 million for 2023 to 2030, which was made permanent in 2024.
quote: Plant-based Food Grant DKK 675 M, 2023 to 2030 (about DKK 84 M a year); made permanent (2024)
notes: Quote is the package's wording (vision benchmarks working paper) of the plan. A secondary source reports DKK 812 million after top-ups (VIS-02); the plan has no KPIs. Denmark also plans a livestock emissions tax from 2030.

claim: The Netherlands' National Growth Fund granted EUR 60 million in April 2022 to a cellular agriculture consortium (cultivated meat and precision fermentation), for a programme running 2023 to 2031.
quote: grants conditional funding of 60 million euros to the Cellular Agriculture consortium
notes: Conditional in April 2022; the Growth Fund page lists it as an active project.

claim: In the UK, the Bezos Earth Fund put USD 30 million into a Bezos Centre for Sustainable Protein at Imperial College London (June 2024), and UKRI put GBP 15 million into a National Alternative Protein Innovation Centre led by Leeds (August 2024).
quote: £15 million from UKRI (BBSRC and Innovate UK), plus £19.3 million in co-investment from over 100 stakeholders
notes: Trade press gives NAPIC as GBP 38 million in total. The Bezos centre is private philanthropy, not public money; a sister centre opened in Singapore (NUS, AFN-15). The UK also allocated an initial GBP 184 million to engineering biology scale-up in 2025 (FTB-24).

claim: The United States launched a National Biotechnology and Biomanufacturing Initiative by Executive Order 14081 in September 2022, but that order was revoked in March 2025.
quote: (k) Executive Order 14081 of September 12, 2022 (Advancing Biotechnology and Biomanufacturing Innovation...)
notes: Revocation published in the Federal Register on 20 March 2025 (90 FR 13037). Whether any NBBI programmes continue under other authorities was not checked.

claim: China's 2025 No. 1 Central Document calls for a 'diversified food supply system', including to 'cultivate and develop biological agriculture and open up new types of food resources'.
quote: 践行大农业观、大食物观，全方位多途径开发食物资源。培育发展生物农业，开拓新型食品资源。
notes: Section (8) of the document dated 1 January 2025, released 23 February 2025. English wording is our translation. The 15th Five-Year Plan wording on 'new types of food' is in app-n (RGN-24; RGN-43; ECF-29).

claim: China's state investor SDIC committed over CNY 4 billion (about USD 555 million) to biomanufacturing in May 2025, with a novel protein centre at Jiangnan University.
quote: a commitment of over CNY 4 billion ($555 million) toward advancing biomanufacturing infrastructure
notes: Disagreement: GFI's global policy report gives about USD 1 billion from SDIC (RGN-43, used in app-n). Not all of it is for food. Give both.

claim: Israel's Innovation Authority put about NIS 49.5 million (USD 15.5 million) into alternative protein in 2025, taking its cumulative alternative protein investment to about NIS 325 million (USD 100 million).
quote: cumulative investments from the IIA in alternative proteins reached approximately NIS 325 million ($100 million)
notes: Figures supplied by the Authority to GFI Israel. Its 2023 release cited over NIS 140 million of alternative protein grants over a decade (VIS-22).

claim: China issued its first new feed ingredient certificate in August 2021 for a bacterial protein made from steel-mill carbon monoxide (Clostridium autoethanogenum protein), produced at 10,000-tonne scale.
quote: 该证书由农业农村部于2021年8月颁发，新饲证字（2021）01号
notes: Producer: Beijing Shougang LanzaTech. The Caofeidian plant makes 5,000 t of protein a year per the same source.

claim: Methane-fed single-cell protein for feed is fragile at scale: Calysseo's 20,000 tonne a year plant in Chongqing, Asia's largest, halted production in 2026, while Unibio plans a 50,000 tonne a year plant in Saudi Arabia for 2028.
quote: a severe shortage of working capital
notes: Calysseo 2025 revenue USD 0.71 million, net loss USD 15.5 million (unaudited); full Chinese feed approval received 2024. Unibio's plant is a plan with a state-linked partner (SIIG); Unibio names Asia as an export market.

claim: India's String Bio makes a methane-derived feed protein of about 70% protein that an expert panel judged safe (self-determined GRAS) for US shrimp feed in 2024; no production scale was published.
quote: approximately 70 percent protein derived from methanotrophic bacteria
notes: Self-determined GRAS is not an FDA letter; the source says crustacean feed. BioMar validated it in salmon feed trials in 2022 (PRC-32).

claim: Insect meal, used here only as a benchmark, has struggled in Europe: Ynsect, Agronutris, Enorm and Inseco failed or restructured, and a major feed maker says insects must beat vegetable proteins on cost and performance.
quote: BioMar: insects 'must outperform vegetable proteins' in cost, performance and sustainability
notes: Quote as recorded in the package source notes. Benchmark only; insect protein is not recommended in this package. Vietnam's Entobel plant has 11,000 t a year design capacity (ECO-01).

claim: About 34% of the world's fishmeal was made from fish processing by-products in 2024, and fishmeal made up about 5.8% of fed aquaculture feed on average in 2017.
quote: 2024: 34% of fishmeal and 54% of fish oil from by-products
notes: Reused from the package (IFFO; Boyd et al. 2022). By-products supplied 54% of fish oil in 2024.

claim: Fishmeal supply tightened in 2026: Peru's first-season anchovy quota was 1.9 million tonnes, 36% below 2025, and world fishmeal output fell 26% in January to April 2026.
quote: Peru's 2026 first-season quota was 1.9 Mt, 36% below 2025 and the lowest in a decade.
notes: Quote is the package horizon-scan wording of HSC-29. Only about a quarter of the quota was landed before the season closed on 21 August 2026.

claim: Singapore, the first country to approve cultivated meat, dropped its '30 by 30' food production goal in November 2025 and left alternative protein out of its 2035 local production targets.
quote: exclude alternative protein 'given the nascency of the sector'
notes: Reused from app-n. Singapore still approved cultivated duck (April 2026) and beef (July 2026).

claim: Thailand's Biotechnology Industry Development Framework 2026 to 2035 names future food and alternative proteins as one of four target sub-industries and plans a shared precision-fermentation pilot plant.
unit: million baht a year for 10 years (synthetic biology research)
quote: 'future food and alternative proteins' is one of four target sub-industries
notes: Reused from app-n. Thailand's first cultivated meat application (Aleph Farms, December 2024) was still unapproved in September 2026 (RGN-32).

claim: South Korea's Food Tech Industry Promotion Act took effect in December 2025 and Korea overtook Singapore as Asia-Pacific's leading base for cultivated meat start-ups, but neither Korea nor Japan (draft guidance only) had approved a cultivated product by September 2026.
quote: Korea ranked fourth-largest cultivated meat ecosystem in the world
notes: Korean applications open since February 2024 (RGN-34); MFDS standards for cell-cultured processed foods June 2026 (FTB-20). Japan: GFI dates draft guidelines to December 2025, app-n records draft safety checkpoints of 28 May 2026 (RGN-33); possibly two stages of one process.

claim: GFI, an advocacy group, counts at least USD 2.5 billion of cumulative government investment in alternative proteins worldwide since 2021.
quote: Cumulative government investment in alternative proteins has reached at least $2.5 billion globally since 2021
notes: Advocacy tally; method not read. GFI APAC words it as 'more than $2.5 billion' in 2025 'up from $700 million in 2021', which reads as cumulative. Do not add to private investment or to the national amounts above.
